for_you_if: you love stylish turn-based combat with deep mechanical layers
you want a massive campaign packed with memorable music
you enjoy distinct dungeons with unique puzzles
not_for_you_if: you need an internet-free experience on portable hardware
you lose patience with prolonged story pacing
you need stable performance without random crashes
you get frustrated by sudden difficulty spikes

citations.review_text:
TL;DR: game is absolute cinema, style leaks through the screen. Go buy it if you haven't played it before

However, DENUVO is a piece of crap. You can't play this game on steam deck without internet connection. So Steam Deck verified is a bit of a white lie: FPS are great but what's the point of you can't play it during commute or a trip.

Jesus Christ, it's been years since it was released. Remove DENUVO crap from this masterpiece already ❤️

DENUVO!!!!

I was playing yesterday just fine and had fun with the game, today I turn on PC and want to go straight into the game and I get
"Currently your game purchase cannot be re-validated successfully, please wait 24 hours and try again."

WTF is this?... Why can't I play game which I've just bought? This is the last time I've purchased anything from you, damn bastards!

claims.claim: Reviewers experience performance issues including random freezing and frame rate dips in intensive areas like the city.

citations.review_text:
Decided to get this even though I've never played this sort of genre at all, but so far - absolutely amazing! Really cool concept, I can tell it dives really deep into its idea, we'll see how good it is down the road! 

Also pretty demanding game for how it looks, and there are 5 second freezes. On a 5070, 1440p 120fps, but can dip (and pretty often does in the city) into the 80fps range in intensive areas.

At first I was hesitant to pick up the game due to the fact that I was tired of seeing so many people talking about how it was the best game in the series. As someone who grew up with persona 3 / P3P I was heavily biased towards that personally and wasn't really a fan of the Shadows being "The true self"- the same reason I was partial to Persona 4 really, but when I finally got around to playing this (I'm not that far as of writing yet), I actually an finding myself very invested in the characters and story. The topics that are handled in this so far are treated realistically and that's kinda scary at points because there ARE times where people get away with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ things until someone steps in and manages to point it out.

It's hard to explain, really, but I just really think it's interesting how the game is handling such heavy topics and making the characters have more depth. 

A main thing I saw people complain about in Persona 3 was the lack of depth in the characters and usually praising 5 for having more, and sadly I do see where they were coming from despite my still strong love for 3 (and P3P remedies alot of the bonds you can't even start unless you're doing the female route, which is lacking in P3R which makes me really sad. I mean there's a mod but it's a bit janky). 

That aside the point is I like the game so far. I do recommend it, but keep in mind it really does go into some hard topics fast. 

However, performance wise I am having issue s with the game freezing VERY often. I managed to fix it by setting it to only use 2 cores of and high priority in task manager, but the main thing that i'm recommended to do (switching to my graphics card for 3d Opengl) is near impossible for me because of my hardware just not letting me change it. That's more a me problem, but it's something I feel I should warn about incase anyone else has the issue.

HOO BOY, Okimura's Palace is the hardest in my experience, absolutely unforgiving in its bosses and puzzles. To think that Atlus would learn their lesson, but no, they did that to Maruki's palace too, lol. 

PS: Somehow got the best ending in the game.
okumura boss and palace gotta die

I really love this game because it has everything you could ask. The soundrack is amazing and made with love , The social links were fun to complete, the palaces were great with fun bossfights (exept okumura's) and Ren is goated he's like the perfect protagonist with unlimited aura. Its almost scary how good this game is and  it makes me crave some delicious pancakes. 
10/10

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players praise the soundtrack and stylish turn-based combat while noting dragged pacing and trivialized late-game challenges.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the soundtrack, highlighting its musical composition and vocal performances.

citations.review_text:
A turn based game to love. With my only criticism being that some of the character stories get pretty sidelined past their relevant location. Despite that, with 106 hours to complete, there is so much to love.

In comparison to other Persona games, I have only played and beaten Persona 3 Reload. While I think Reload has the better cast, that doesn't mean this one is bad, they're still a lot of fun and lovable (Morgana is debatable, Makoto is queen) with some characters who REALLY stand out compared to Reload (Akechi is amazing), and it doesn't matter which you start first. The gameplay is definitely better in this one, because you are thank god not clearing floor after floor after floor as almost the entire premise of the game like Reload. Worth my time, worth my money, changed my view of things.

Also the soundtrack is a GEM like every Persona game.
A fantastic game. Killer soundtrack!

Persona 5 Royal completely lived up to the hype for me.

The first thing that grabbed me was the style. Everything from the menus to the battle system is packed with personality. Even doing simple things feels cool because of how incredibly stylish the presentation is. It's one of those games where you can tell every little detail was made with care.

The combat is a blast. Chaining together weaknesses, Baton Passes, All-Out Attacks, and making the most of your Personas is really satisfying, and battles stay fun throughout the game without feeling repetitive.

The story and characters are easily some of the best I've experienced. I did see a couple of the twists coming, but honestly that didn't take away from the impact at all. The characters are so well written and the setting is so engaging that I was invested the whole way through. And even though I guessed a few things, there were still plenty of moments that completely caught me off guard and genuinely blew me away.

The soundtrack is also fantastic. There are so many memorable tracks, and quite a few have made their way into my everyday playlists. Lyn's vocals are a huge part of what gives the game its identity and really elevate a lot of the games moments.

Persona 5 Royal is one of those games where the gameplay, story, music, and presentation all come together incredibly well. It's an easy recommendation from me.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game's pacing drags and portions of the story feel overstuffed or drawn out.

citations.review_text: I played the original persona 5 back in 2018 on the PS4, and I loved it then. In fact it gave me a reason to delve into persona 4 which I never played before and by that result revisiting persona 3 with reload which I didn't like that much in my youth. This game is a great game that I think most if not all fans of RPGs should try at some point. However, upon playing 3 and 4, and replaying this with the Royal content, it made me see the cracks in the otherwise perfect game design. The biggest offender is the pacing, it really drags in some areas compared to 3 and 4. I do however believe that with the 120 hours I spent (118 on my first playthrough on the PS4) I still can't deny this might be one of the better starting points for would-be fans. I also, through becoming a fan of the series and the knowledge that comes with it, completed this playthrough by getting all of the achievements in one playthrough only using guides to optimize confidant answers. I did EVERYTHING and that made me feel incredibly proud of myself. Enough jabbering, if you are on the fence, make the leap towards the truth and steal those distorted hearts...It's worth it.

Persona 5 Royal is a deeply flawed game. Most obviously regarding its length -- the plot is hopelessly overstuffed, progressing at a snail's pace, and it has like, three final bosses. And for a lot of its 115 hour runtime, the story is unremarkable: most of the antagonists are one-note mustache-twirling villains of the week, and outside of them, there is very little friction from the game's cast. The Phantom Thieves express very little individual agency after they join the team; they're more of a hivemind revolving around you, and every adult side character's story follows a pretty formulaic structure. On top of that, the game is easy as sin -- the player is given so many tools, you'll only really be challenged for the first two dungeons at most, and that's assuming you opt out of using the formerly-DLC Personas now unlocked by default in this release of the game. 

With all that being said, though... I really like it anyway. The social sim/dungeon crawler hybrid formula established in Persona 3 feels like it was [b]made[/b] for a high school-superhero story, and though much praise has already been sung for P5's famously singular aesthetic identity and soundtrack (emulated by many, equaled by few), it cannot be overstated how [i]good[/i] every single action feels in this game -- ranking up confidants, chaining Baton Passes, completing Challenge Battles in the Velvet Room, or even watching the progress reports pile up whenever you exit a Palace; it's like straight dopamine shots to my brain in a positive feedback loop. Speaking of, both the nine Palaces and the six real-world free roam maps are caringly constructed and evocative to explore, and the Thieves' Den is one of the most underrated extras menus in any game. The slow crawl of days into weeks into months immerses the player in a way few games do, and the characters you spend that time with are near-universally endearing, thanks in no small part to the great performances in the English dub. And though I complai…

Pretty fun game. My main complaint is that the last ~15% of the game (including the new Royal content) is dragged out considerably. There's too much filler dialogue for my tastes (even as a VN enjoyer) but some people will enjoy that aspect a lot.

Persona 5 Royal is a 100+ hour masterpiece that takes an already incredible game and polishes it to perfection. You play as a high schooler living a double life: navigating classes, exams, and friendships by day, and leading a supernatural heist crew—the Phantom Thieves—by night to change the hearts of corrupt adults.

This definitive edition doesn't just add fluff; it overhauls the experience with massive quality-of-life improvements, a new grappling hook for dungeon exploration, and an entirely new third semester that features arguably the best storyline in the game. New characters like Kasumi and Maruki integrate perfectly into the original plot, adding emotional weight and fantastic new abilities.

It retains the wildly stylish art direction, incredibly fun turn-based combat, and an unforgettable acid-jazz soundtrack. If you have the time to commit, this is one of the best JRPGs ever made.

The best Persona in terms of gameplay and variation, with a host of mechanics and QOL features that seperate it as a mechanical experience from previous Persona titles. While the story does not hit the heights of Persona 3, it is probably the 2nd best in the series and has a host of memorable characters and moments.

Definitely worth your money, just make sure to set aside a hundred hours or so as well.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features distinct palace environments with interactive puzzles tied to different characters.

citations.review_text:
What an amazing game. I started my Persona journey almost a year ago to this day. I played through Persona 4 Golden, Persona 3 Reload and now, Persona 5 Royal. It has been an amazing experience to play these games. This game takes what made the series great and expands it to the next level. 

First off, is the combat and dungeon experience. In this game, dungeons are stylized depending on what character's palace you are in. The music, environment and enemies change as well. There are also puzzles in the dungeons which make them feel more important as they are very interactive. The combat itself is also very nice. As usual, each enemy has certain elements they are strong against and weak against, as do your personas. However, this game adds a cool feature called the baton pass. When you hit an enemy's weakness, you are able to gain an extra turn and you pass this turn to someone else on your team. This gives them health, sp, and extra damage. This concept made strategizing within your team much more important and added more layers of combat to the game. Boss fights in this game were also very enjoyable. Each boss had unique phases and they all felt like appropriate challenges without becoming too difficult or too easy. I also liked the fact that in each palace or Mementos you could capture the enemy you were fighting and it became your persona. That feature was really cool. Overall, combat and dungeons are the best in the series and take what was great in previous games and expand on it.

Presentation. It is important that every game has a stylized feel and sound to it. This game delivers on all points, starting with the UI. It is very clean. So so clean. It is red and black sort of comic style. Each menu has cool animation to it and background. It feels very intuitive and easy to use. In battle, everything you need you can see on the screen, and it's all mapped to individual buttons in combat so you never have to look hard to figure out where something is. The trans…

This game is excellent in a lot of ways, while it has its flaws I enjoyed almost every second of playing! I am in love with it, and it deserves all the attention it gets. I feel like I robbed Atlus buying this on a steam sale for 70% off 

This is a non spoiler tip: max social links for Maruki and get Akech to 8, Kasumi to level 5, and Max Hifumi and Kawakami. Most of the other social links are amazing too but keep these ones in mind 100000% you will regret it for abilities and other reasons. 

Non spoiler review ahead:

Nearly 200 hours, a bad ending and a true ending later I can say this game is full of heart. I will be gushing positives first but scroll down for the few cons. 

The turn based battle system is SO FUN! So many creative moves, ideas, and concepts that lean into the 'villanous' thieves you're supposed to be. Each themed dunegon is creative as well, with different puzzles that vary from fun easy to fun difficult.

The characters are fantastic with so many creative designs, distinct personalities that all come together with EXCELLENT voice acting. I played in english, and I'd list the whole cast if I could but they all do an amazing job. I can't think of a time I skipped anything not just for plot but because I couldn't bring myself to skip any of the preformances. 

The graphics are wonderful too. I know P3R and the upcoming P4R look even better, but P5R hasn't aged poorly at all. The graphics are pretty and charming as time goes on. Additionally, the music is TOP tier but I don't have to explain that once you start playing lol. The tasks to do outside of dunegons is also great. There is a variety of things to do and stats to increase all while exploring the immersive enviroments the game offers you. This game really emphazies taking your time, and I think you should! There is so much to do and enjoy that this game isn't fit for a speedrun of any kind. 

P5R is also full of great characters and great writing. Many of the social links are amazing, and …

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as fast-paced, stylish, and featuring mechanics like Baton Passes for chaining turns.

citations.review_text: A masterpiece of JRPG, a wonderful entry to persona series for newcomers who want to experience the charm of JRPG. Persona 5 Royal brings a fresh look on the traditional turn-based style by providing players with flashy, fast-paced combat and a very unique menu design which is a huge selling point of the game. The game brings me back to good old high school days (2 years ago :D) and expose me to in-depth cast of characters, a few of them actually resonates with my circumstances so much that left a lasting impression on me for quite a while. Not to mention, the theme of Persona 5 is extremely fascinating and, in a way, positively affect my own outlook on life and how I would face unfair situations with a rebellious stance. Overall, I believe 10/10 would be very fitting for this work of art.

I wished I'd have played this game much sooner. I've heard great things about it for years but I've only played it recently, but I'm glad that I did end up playing this great game. It has a really cool premise and story about Japanese high school students standing up for what they believe in and changing society for the better. It also covers the challenges that such a group would face and the mistakes they would inevitably make. I like the characters a well, they very distinct and very realistically written. The protagonists feel like they have a good reason to do what they do and the antagonists are very evil in a realistic way. The gameplay is also really fun, I like how this game does its turn-based combat, although it is a little too easy. I also was surprised by how much I like the social sim elements of the game. The confidant stories are really engaging and I love how what you do in the real world ties into what you can do in the dungeon-crawling parts of the game. It does have some problems though, some of the "humor " is painfully unfunny and some of the anime-style fan-service can get in the way of my enjoyment of the game. And I think it is really strange how you can have the main protagonist, a teenager, date four adult women, one of which is his teacher. But while those parts exist, they're not enough to ruin my enjoyment of this game. If you are an RPG fan with tons of spare time, I would 100% recommend this game.

The soundtrack is also fantastic. There are so many memorable tracks, and quite a few have made their way into my everyday playlists. Lyn's vocals are a huge part of what gives the game its identity and really elevate a lot of the games moments.

Persona 5 Royal is one of those games where the gameplay, story, music, and presentation all come together incredibly well. It's an easy recommendation from me.

citations.review_text: I'd definitely recommend this game to anyone interested in immersive storytelling. The characters' behavior is kinda ridiculous at times in a simply irritating way — like shouting about being a Phantom Thief in public, even though the character himself had already pointed out that it's completely out of touch. The game's graphic style is truly pleasant to the eye, but the UI itself leaves a lot to be desired, especially in the Velvet Room. Despite way too many unexplained mechanics, it's a very well-made game.

Persona 5 Royal is a deeply flawed game. Most obviously regarding its length -- the plot is hopelessly overstuffed, progressing at a snail's pace, and it has like, three final bosses. And for a lot of its 115 hour runtime, the story is unremarkable: most of the antagonists are one-note mustache-twirling villains of the week, and outside of them, there is very little friction from the game's cast. The Phantom Thieves express very little individual agency after they join the team; they're more of a hivemind revolving around you, and every adult side character's story follows a pretty formulaic structure. On top of that, the game is easy as sin -- the player is given so many tools, you'll only really be challenged for the first two dungeons at most, and that's assuming you opt out of using the formerly-DLC Personas now unlocked by default in this release of the game. 

With all that being said, though... I really like it anyway. The social sim/dungeon crawler hybrid formula established in Persona 3 feels like it was [b]made[/b] for a high school-superhero story, and though much praise has already been sung for P5's famously singular aesthetic identity and soundtrack (emulated by many, equaled by few), it cannot be overstated how [i]good[/i] every single action feels in this game -- ranking up confidants, chaining Baton Passes, completing Challenge Battles in the Velvet Room, or even watching the progress reports pile up whenever you exit a Palace; it's like straight dopamine shots to my brain in a positive feedback loop. Speaking of, both the nine Palaces and the six real-world free roam maps are caringly constructed and evocative to explore, and the Thieves' Den is one of the most underrated extras menus in any game. The slow crawl of days into weeks into months immerses the player in a way few games do, and the characters you spend that time with are near-universally endearing, thanks in no small part to the great performances in the English dub.
